messages:

Subject: Post-call: integration checklist + ask (auth, routing, structured output)

Hi Evan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned from a technical POV:

- Goal from BrightPay: embed a candidate-ranking pipeline in payroll reconciliation (embeddings -> reranker -> structured tool call to HR system).
- Primary constraints you shared: strict 10s API timeout on your side for initial call, and company policy requires request metadata be logged locally (request_id + user_id).

Immediate asks we have so our eng team can reproduce: please send
1) an example request payload your client sends to Redwood (headers + body) — include SDK version if you can;
2) any logs (request id, timestamp) from the 5xx you hit today;
3) which environment/region you hit (us-west/us-east).

I’ve looped Marcus (serving/runtime) and Monica (solutions eng) to help with repro and recommended changes for timeouts/structured output. Tentative plan once we get payload+logs:
- Marcus: reproduce in staging, confirm whether 5xx is a routing/auth issue or payload-triggered (large JSON embed + nested toolcall).
- Monica: propose immediate mitigations (client-side timeout bump + client-side retry/backoff guidance).
- Aisha: schedule a 30-minute follow-up to review repro and canary tests.

Would you be able to drop the payload + one sample 5xx log into this thread by EOD? If it helps, you can attach files to reply or paste a sanitized JSON.

Thanks — speak soon.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Aisha — attaching what I can. Quick notes:

- Environment: us-west-2 (we hit your hosted endpoint in that region).
- SDK: our client is using brightpay/redwood-js v0.9.2 (we'll try v1.0.0 next).
- Symptoms: when we send a combined request (embeddings + synchronous reranker + tool call metadata) we see intermittent 502/502-ish 5xx responses. Mostly at peak payroll runs.

Attached: brightpay_request_payload.json (sanitized), brightpay_5xx-log.txt, screenshot-502.png

Relevant payload excerpt (sanitized):
{
  "model": "reranker-large-v1",
  "input": {
    "documents": [ /* ~80 small docs, combined size ~120KB */ ],
    "query": "match employee transactions to ledger entries"
  },
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "hr-lookup",
      "params": { "employee_id": "{{user_id}}" }
    }
  ],
  "client_meta": { "request_id": "bp-20270514-9421", "user_id": "e.liu" }
}

We also see that increasing the client timeout to 30s reduces incidents, but that’s not acceptable for our product SLA. We're hoping Redwood can identify whether this is a server-side routing/kv-cache saturation issue, or a request-size parsing problem.

Anything else you need? We can open a short call with devs if it helps.

—Evan

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Post-call: integration checklist + ask (auth, routing, structured output)

Hi Evan — thanks for the payload and logs; these are super helpful. Quick diagnosis and proposed repro steps below. Short version: initial repro points to a routing/KV cache pressure on the reranker path when a large documents array is included + synchronous tool call metadata.

What I did (staging):
1) Replayed your payload against staging model variant (reranker-large-v1.quant) with 80 docs (120KB total).
2) Observed connection spike and a backend worker returning 502 when the reranker attempted to allocate KV pages for the full sequence during cross-attention. Trace id 7c2f-rr-20270514 (we’ll map to your request ids with debug headers).

Immediate mitigation (doable quickly on your side):
- Client change: split the document batch into chunks of ~20 docs per request and aggregate reranker scores client-side (you can parallelize these requests to stay within the 10s perceived latency) — this avoids a single huge sequence KV expansion.
- Timeout: temporarily bump client-side to 20s for retryable requests; implement exponential backoff (100ms -> 500ms -> 2s) for transient 5xx.
- Headers: add X-RW-Debug: true and include Redwood-Request-Id header (we’ll provide mapping) so we can trace server-side logs to your request IDs.

Server-side actions we will take this week:
- Run a targeted canary on staging with a workload closer to your doc-size distribution and validate whether kernel fallback is causing the 502.
- Add a short-term routing guard to refuse a single-request document batch over 200KB with a clear 413-like error (better than an opaque 502).

Repro steps for you (minimal):
- Send one of your original request payloads with header Redwood-Request-Id: bp-20270514-9421 and X-RW-Debug: true to staging endpoint https://staging.api.redwood.inference/v1/generate (I can create a staging token for your team).
- If you can, paste one full raw request_id from your logs into this thread and mark which timestamp corresponds to the 5xx.

I’ve attached a short runbook we’ll use internally to triage (I put it on the Drive link in related_links). I’ll coordinate with infra to prioritize the canary. Monica, can you share a quick client-side sample to chunk and aggregate?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

1) BrightPay: please reply with one raw request_id from your brightpay_5xx-log.txt and confirm whether you can run a single test against staging with the headers Marcus listed (Redwood-Request-Id + X-RW-Debug). If you want a staging token, let me know and I’ll issue one. (Due today if possible)
2) BrightPay: try a temp client change to chunk to 20-doc batches for peak runs and report whether that eliminates the 502s (we expect positive impact). (Due by EOD Monday)
3) Redwood: Marcus will run the staging canary and push a routing guard to return a clear 413-like response for too-large batch payloads (internal ETA: 48–72 hours).
4) Follow-up call: I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical sync next Tue 11am PT to review canary results and agree on a production rollout plan.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick collaboration. Evan, feel free to call my mobile if something pops up: +1 (415) 555-0214.

Best,
